newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buyers sidelined in N.Europe rapeseed market.
newsitem.headline: Buyers sidelined in N.Europe rapeseed market.

text.p: Traders and crushers are shunning rapeseed in Europe although it offers a cheap alternative to soybeans and sunseed, brokers said.

This was because old crop material was hard to find and crushers were not yet convinced of profitable markets for rape meal and oil in the summer months, when new crop seed becomes available, they said.
Weekend rain in western Euroved crop prospects and this also acted as a psychological disincentive.
"Crush margins could improve nearer the harvest, especially if the crop looks good, and crushers have put off buying decisions until later," one broker said.
"But it could be the wrong strategy when you look at today's prices -- July/Aug rapeseed offers are at around $272, soybeans at $340 and sunflower at $320."
Free Hamburg old crop buyers were at 510 marks a tonne, in the middle of the national 500-520 range taken from destinations other than Hamburg.
New crop free Hamburg (August) buyers were at 465 marks and sellers at 470, versus a national 440-460 buying range.
Traders and producers of new crop started negotiations on pre-harvest contracts in western Germany.
In the East of the country, sizeable lots have already been sold to country merchants and co-ops. Farmgate prices in the region were put at 440 marks.
Aug rapeseed futures on the Matif exchange last traded at 464 marks, down one from Friday's close.
Spot April rape meal ex Hamburg mills was offered at a steady 32.00-32.25 marks per 100 kg, with May at 32.00 and June/first half July at 30.75.
Rape oil sellers were one mark up on the week on May at 94.50 marks per 100 kg, with Aug/Oct oil up three marks at 95.50.
